claims.statement: The galasa-boot JAR is the primary entry point for launching Galasa in various operational modes including test execution, API server, metrics server, resource management, Kubernetes controller, and ecosystem setup.
After building the framework locally, the galasa-boot JAR is located at galasa/modules/framework/galasa-parent/galasa-boot/build/libs/galasa-boot-{version}.jar.
The boot JAR validates that Java 17 is available on startup and exits with an error if an incompatible Java version is detected.
The --obr option specifies OSGi Bundle Repositories to load, supporting multiple repositories through repeated use of the flag.
The --bootstrap option accepts a URL to bootstrap properties starting with http:// or file://, with a 30-second connection and read timeout.
The --overrides option accepts a URL to overrides properties starting with http:// or file://, and defaults to ${GALASA_HOME}/overrides.properties if the file exists.
The --test option executes a specific test class using the format {osgi-bundle-name}/{fully-qualified-class-name}.
The --methods option allows specifying which test methods to run and can be provided multiple times or as a comma-separated list.
The --run option executes a test by run name, converting the name to uppercase automatically.
The --gherkin option runs a Gherkin test specification from a file:// URL.
The --api option starts the Galasa REST API server by loading Jetty bundles and invoking ApiStartup.run().
The --resourcemanagement option starts the resource management server which monitors and manages resource allocation.
The --local-resource-management option starts a local resource management process supporting includes and excludes glob patterns for resource monitors.
The --k8scontroller option starts the Kubernetes-based engine controller service by loading dev.galasa.framework.k8s.controller and invoking K8sController.run().
The --metricserver option starts the metrics collection service, automatically loading all bundles providing IMetricsProvider services from the OBR.
The --setupeco option sets up a Galasa ecosystem by invoking SetupEcosystem.setup().
The --validateeco option validates a Galasa ecosystem by submitting a CoreManagerIVT test run through ValidateEcosystem.setup().
The --prepare option downloads all OBR bundle dependencies to the local Maven cache without running tests by resolving non-uber OBR bundles and installing them to trigger the Maven URL handler.
The --localmaven option specifies the local Maven repository URL, defaulting to ~/.m2/repository, and supports --localmaven disable to disable local Maven.
The --remotemaven option specifies remote Maven repository URLs, can be provided multiple times, and defaults to Maven Central.
The --offline option disables all remote Maven repository access and cannot be used with --remotemaven.
The --bundle option loads extra bundles beyond those in the OBR and can be provided multiple times.
The --metrics option specifies the metrics server port, with 0 disabling metrics.
The --health option specifies the health check server port, with 0 disabling health checks.
The --trace option enables TRACE-level logging and sets log4j2.configurationFile to trace-log4j2.properties.
The --log4j2-properties-file option accepts a file:// URL or filesystem path to a custom log4j2 properties file and overrides the --trace option.
The GALASA_HOME environment variable or system property controls the Galasa home directory, with precedence order: system property, environment variable, then ${HOME}/.galasa default.
Environment variables GALASA_CONFIG_STORE, GALASA_DYNAMICSTATUS_STORE, GALASA_RESULTARCHIVE_STORE, GALASA_CREDENTIALS_STORE, and GALASA_AUTH_STORE override bootstrap properties for store locations.
Environment variables GALASA_MAVEN_USERNAME and GALASA_MAVEN_PASSWORD set Maven repository credentials in bootstrap properties as maven.repository.username and maven.repository.password.
The GALASA_EXTRA_BUNDLES environment variable specifies a comma-separated list of extra bundles to load, written to framework.extra.bundles in bootstrap properties.
Environment variables GALASA_MONITOR_STREAM, GALASA_MONITOR_INCLUDES_GLOB_PATTERNS, and GALASA_MONITOR_EXCLUDES_GLOB_PATTERNS configure resource management behavior.
The boot JAR initializes Apache Felix OSGi framework with a unique cache directory under ${GALASA_HOME}/cache/felix-cache-{uuid}, which is automatically deleted when the framework stops.
The boot JAR embeds core dependencies including Felix framework, Felix Bundle Repository, Commons CLI, Commons IO, and log4j2 layout template JSON.
The launcher loads core bundles in a specific order: Felix SCR, log4j2 components, Maven repository handlers, then Felix OBR bundle.
The launcher masks DGALASA_JWT values in command-line log output for security.
Service invocation uses OSGi service references and Java reflection to locate and call appropriate service methods with Properties parameters.
